domain: Finite compositions of the separately admitted point, derivative, root-discovery, guard-retention, join-correspondence and dependent-fiber increments, preserving every predecessor fixture and native format migration.
input: u>0,8u^2=1; v>0,16v^3=u; positive graph y^2=x evaluated at x=v. Its retained ordinate is a parameter of C(t)=(t,t^2), whose derivative must be (1,2t); evaluating y=x^2 at half that derivative ordinate must recover v.

preconditions: A private, unqualified integration candidate may be assembled in a separate checkout from immutable source snapshots whose focused acceptance and strict MSRV checks pass. Final integration admission still requires all six source increments to complete their own frozen local/downstream qualifications, final parent alignment and local evidence commits, plus qualification of the combined source. Compatibility review and metadata merging must retain all records. This permits early fault discovery without crediting incomplete validation as admission.
acceptance: Reproduce the two cross-increment failures on the final fiber source and preserve its source control. After integration run every predecessor acceptance fixture, the new chains, fresh-process replay, exact incidence/domain/certainty assertions, small-budget retries and affected full downstream validation. Code and evidence receipts need their own post-edit checks.
publication: No push until the integrated commit passes the full repository pre-push contract. The older parent publication gate is independent.
limits: The original seven implicit-region offset/corner fixtures remain open. Integration is not evidence of universal operation closure or total resource bounds. No speedup is claimed.
